content: Fakir Technologies Ltd. has signed an agreement with FKL Spinning Mills Ltd. for the implementation of a 6.13 MWp On-grid Solar Power Project, in collaboration with Solar EPC Development Ltd. The agreement marks a significant milestone in the journey towards delivering large-scale renewable energy solutions and supporting sustainable industrial development in Bangladesh. With an estimated first-year electricity generation of 8,238 MWh, the project is expected to avoid approximately 5,520 tonnes of CO₂ emissions annually. For FKL Spinning Mills Ltd., this initiative represents a major step towards reducing its environmental footprint, strengthening energy sustainability and embracing cleaner energy alternatives. For Fakir Technologies Ltd., the project further demonstrates its growing capabilities in delivering large-scale renewable energy solutions for the industrial sector. Since 2022, the company has been actively operating in Bangladesh's solar energy and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) sectors, building its expertise through global technology partnerships, project execution and integrated energy solutions. The project is being undertaken by Fakir Technologies Ltd., with Solar EPC Development Ltd. serving as its EPC partner. This 6.13 MWp project further reinforces Fakir Technologies' commitment to supporting industries in their transition towards cleaner, more efficient and sustainable energy systems. The agreement signing ceremony was held at Fakir Knitwears Ltd., Narayanganj, in the presence of senior leadership from both organizations. Noble supplies proprietary materials technologies for applications in apparel, […] The post Americhem acquires Noble Biomaterials appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .
content: US-based polymer specialist Americhem has acquired Noble Biomaterials, the developer of antimicrobial and conductive technologies for textiles and other soft surface applications. The acquisition brings Noble’s specialist technologies into Americhem’s global operations, strengthening the ability to support customers from initial product development through to commercial-scale production. Noble supplies proprietary materials technologies for applications in apparel, textiles, healthcare, aerospace and defence. Its established Ionic+, X-Static and Circuitex platforms provide antimicrobial, odour control and electrical conductivity functions, supported by US manufacturing operations and an extensive intellectual property portfolio developed over more than two decades. The acquisition will strengthen Americhem’s position in functional fibres and polymer solutions, particularly in healthcare and other markets requiring advanced material performance. “This is an exciting step forward for Americhem as we continue to invest in high-growth, high-demand markets,” said Americhem CEO John Richard. “Noble Biomaterials brings exceptional capabilities in antimicrobial solutions, strong commercial relationships and a reputation for quality that aligns with our values.” The financial terms of the acquisition were not disclosed. www.americhem.com www.noblebiomaterials.com The post Americhem acquires Noble Biomaterials appeared first on Innovation in Textiles .

content: Three developments in lightweight construction, automated manufacturing and advanced fibre reinforcement have taken first places in the three categories of the 2026 AVK Innovation Awards, presented at the JEC Composites Talks DACH held in Cologne, Germany, on October 20th. Organised by AVK, the German Federation of Reinforced Plastics, the annual awards recognise advances in composite products, manufacturing processes and scientific research. Products and applications Dresden-based Anybrid secured first place in the products and applications category for a heavy-duty diamond core drill incorporating a carbon fibre-reinforced thermoplastic body in place of conventional steel. Developed with partners including Avanco Composites, Mitsui Chemicals Europe, AFPT, Hilti Kunststofftechnik and TU Dresden, the component has combined laser-based tape winding with injection moulding to produce a lightweight structure with integrated metal connections. The resulting drill assembly achieves a weight reduction of approximately 70% compared with steel, at least doubles service life and reduces its carbon footprint by around 37%. The development has successfully completed mechanical testing and practical field trials. Processes and manufacturing CompriseTec won the processes and methods category for a robotic manufacturing technology that eliminates the need for conventional moulds when producing thermoplastic composite components. title: BAPEX discovers 97.69 BCF gas well in Noakhali
summary: Bangladesh Petroleum Exploration and Production Company Limited (BAPEX) has discovered an estimated 97.69 BCF of natural gas at the Sundalpur South-1 exploratory well in Noakhali’s Companiganj. The di...
content: Bangladesh Petroleum Exploration and Production Company Limited (BAPEX) has discovered an estimated 97.69 BCF of natural gas at the Sundalpur South-1 exploratory well in Noakhali’s Companiganj. The discovery is expected to strengthen local energy security and support efforts to reduce dependence on imported fuels. Courtesy: Collected The discovery was confirmed on 2 November through a gas flare test after drilling operations at the well in Rampur Union were completed. According to BAPEX, the estimated gas reserves are spread across two zones of the well. The gas is valued at approximately Tk 5,809 crore at consumer-level prices, while the well is expected to supply 15 million cubic feet of gas per day to the national grid. Gas extraction from the well is expected to continue for the next 20 years. Drilling at the Sundalpur South-1 exploratory well began on 8 July this year using BAPEX's Bijoy-10 rig. The operation reached a depth of 3,289 meters and was financed jointly by the government and BAPEX. The Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources undertook the drilling initiative based on the findings of BAPEX's three-dimensional (3D) seismic survey. Mohammad Mozammel Haque, Project Director of the Sundalpur South-1 exploratory well, confirmed the discovery. He said further observation and a Drill Stem Test (DST) over the next 15 days would determine whether oil or any other substance is also present in the well. The discovery comes as Bangladesh continues to explore domestic gas resources to strengthen energy security and reduce dependence on imported fuels.

Despite acknowledging the challenges, experts agreed that the target is achievable if bureaucratic obstacles are removed and financing mechanisms are strengthened. However, they emphasized that success will depend not only on installing solar panels but also on developing a skilled workforce, upgrading the electricity grid and ensuring long-term maintenance. Dipal C Barua, Founder and Chairman of Bright Green Energy Foundation, stressed the need to prioritize decentralized renewable energy alongside conventional power generation. content: Dhaka, 3 November 2026: Fakir Technologies Ltd. has signed an agreement with FKL Spinning Mills Ltd. for the implementation of a 6.13 MWp On-grid Solar Power Project , in collaboration with Solar EPC Development Ltd. The agreement marks a significant milestone in the journey towards delivering large-scale renewable energy solutions and supporting sustainable industrial development in Bangladesh. With an estimated first-year electricity generation of 8,238 MWh , the project is expected to avoid approximately 5,520 tonnes of CO ₂ emissions annually . For FKL Spinning Mills Ltd., this initiative represents a major step towards reducing its environmental footprint, strengthening energy sustainability and embracing cleaner energy alternatives. For Fakir Technologies Ltd., the project further demonstrates its growing capabilities in delivering large-scale renewable energy solutions for the industrial sector. Since 2022, the company has been actively operating in Bangladesh’s solar energy and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) sectors, building its expertise through global technology partnerships, project execution and integrated energy solutions. The project is being undertaken by Fakir Technologies Ltd., with Solar EPC Development Ltd. serving as its EPC partner. This 6.13 MWp project further reinforces Fakir Technologies’ commitment to supporting industries in their transition towards cleaner, more efficient and sustainable energy systems. The agreement signing ceremony was held at Fakir Knitwears Ltd., Narayanganj , in the presence of senior leadership from both organizations. Held at the Oregon Convention Center from 26-28 October, the event attracted its highest attendance to date, up 7% compared with […] The post Functional Fabric Fair reaches new heights appeared first on Knitting Industry .
content: Functional Fabric Fair powered by Performance Days has reported record attendance at its Fall 2026 edition in Portland, reinforcing its growing importance as an international sourcing and innovation platform for the performance textiles industry. Held at the Oregon Convention Center from 26-28 October, the event attracted its highest attendance to date, up 7% compared with Fall 2025. The exhibition hall sold out with more than 350 exhibitors, while the opening OIA Catalyst Conference also reached capacity, bringing together more than 300 industry professionals. The results reflect the increasing significance of Functional Fabric Fair and its partnership with Performance Days, which together provide an expanding international platform connecting textile manufacturers, technology developers, apparel brands and sourcing professionals. With an established presence in Europe through Performance Days in Munich and a growing programme of Functional Fabric Fair events across the United States, the partnership is strengthening its position as a year-round meeting point for the global functional textiles industry. content: When the Factory Stops, Everyone’s Clock Keeps Running Imagine a factory on a November morning. Fabric is ready. Some garments are waiting for their final inspection. A merchandiser opens an email from a buyer: “Can you confirm the shipment date?” Outside, workers are gathering. Inside, management is deciding whether production can continue safely. The shipment clock is still running. So is the worker’s rent. So is the factory’s interest bill Figure: Ruhul Talukder, Managing Director, Ruhrose.com That is what makes Bangladesh’s current garment crisis so difficult. People standing on different sides of the factory gate are worried about the same thing: their future. The challenge is finding a way forward that they can trust. Behind the headlines are two kinds of pressure: Workers are demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000. Their protests also include concerns about blacklisting and the reinstatement of dismissed workers. Reports of road blockades, clashes and attacks on property show how serious the situation has become. For workers, the discussion starts with daily life: food, rent, transport and the cost of supporting a family. For factory owners, it starts with a different calculation: the price agreed with the buyer, the cost of materials, wages, energy and the money left after shipment. Neither calculation disappears because the other side is struggling. A worker cannot pay rent with an explanation about low margins. A factory cannot meet a higher wage bill simply by wishing buyers would pay more. This is where leadership matters. The industry needs a workable agreement that recognises both realities. content: In an exclusive interview at TITAS 2026, Justin Huang, President of the Taiwan Textile Federation (TTF), discusses the material innovations and commercial decisions behind Taiwan’s drive to recover more value from textile waste. By Nithin Kumar A performance fabric earns its reputation through what it does for the wearer. For Justin Huang, its value increasingly extends to what happens after use: whether its materials can be recovered and made useful again. Justin Huang, President of the Taiwan Textile Federation (TTF) Speaking exclusively to The Textile Magazine at the 30th Taipei Innovative Textile Application Show, TITAS 2026, Huang argues that material recovery can strengthen Taiwan’s position with global brands. With relatively high labour and energy costs, he says, Taiwanese suppliers must give international customers compelling reasons to choose them. He points to years of investment in materials and manufacturing processes intended to reduce environmental impact. In his account, taking responsibility for textile waste is becoming part of the value Taiwan offers its customers. Giving textiles another life A central priority is the move beyond PET-bottle recycling towards textile-to-textile recycling. Garments commonly combine different fibres, complicating the recovery process. Materials must be identified and sorted, while dyes and other unwanted substances may need to be removed. title: US trade show returns to Dhaka with $5 billion investment target
summary: The United States is seeking to expand its business and investment engagement with Bangladesh as the American Chamber of Commerce in Bangladesh (AmCham) prepares to host the 30th US Trade Show in Dhak...
content: The United States is seeking to expand its business and investment engagement with Bangladesh as the American Chamber of Commerce in Bangladesh (AmCham) prepares to host the 30th US Trade Show in Dhaka from November 5 to 7. The event comes as both countries look to strengthen trade relations, attract new investment and expand cooperation in technology, energy and manufacturing. The American Chamber of Commerce in Bangladesh holds a special press conference ahead of the ‘30th US Trade Show 2026’ at the Hotel InterContinental in the capital on November 2. | The three-day exhibition will take place at Hotel InterContinental Dhaka after a gap of two and a half years. It will showcase American products, services and technologies while providing a platform for business networking and investment discussions. AmCham announced the event at a press conference on November 2. According to the organizers, 43 exhibitors, including 36 companies and seven startups, will participate through 63 booths. Syed Mohammad Kamal, President, AmCham, said the chamber had previously set a target of attracting $5 billion in US investment to Bangladesh over the next five years. He emphasized that energy security would be essential to achieving this goal. "If this exhibition helps bring 10 to 12 new American companies to Bangladesh, that itself will be a major achievement," he said. The investment target comes against a backdrop of expanding bilateral economic relations. According to the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR), total US-Bangladesh goods and services trade reached an estimated $13.7 billion in 2025, increasing 10.3% from 2024. title: Wage protests disrupt operations at over 300 garment factories
summary: Garment manufacturing operations faced disruptions across major industrial zones in Gazipur, Ashulia and Mirpur on Tuesday as workers continued demonstrations demanding higher wages. More than 300 fac...
content: Garment manufacturing operations faced disruptions across major industrial zones in Gazipur, Ashulia and Mirpur on Tuesday as workers continued demonstrations demanding higher wages. More than 300 factories announced temporary holidays or experienced production stoppages amid the ongoing situation. Courtesy: Collected According to the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA), 161 factories in Gazipur declared general holidays, while production remained suspended at 93 factories in the Savar, Ashulia and Zirani areas. Another 52 factories were also reported closed following work stoppages by workers. In Gazipur, demonstrations took place at several industrial locations, including Naojor, Bhogra, Palli Bidyut and Chandra. Workers attempted to block sections of the Dhaka-Tangail Highway, affecting traffic movement between Joydebpur Chowrasta and Naojor. Additional law enforcement personnel were deployed to manage the situation and maintain traffic flow. Similar disruptions were reported in Ashulia, where workers gathered at several points along the Baipail-Abdullahpur road. Although many workers initially joined their regular shifts, some factories subsequently suspended operations as a precautionary measure amid concerns over possible disruptions. The situation also affected industrial activity in Mirpur, where workers staged demonstrations in the Mirpur 11 area. Police and other security personnel were deployed in the affected locations to maintain order and facilitate a return to normal activities. content: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman joined the opening ceremony of Bangladesh Solar Expo-2026 in the city this morning as the chief guest. The inaugural ceremony began at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre in the capital, said Prime Minister’s Deputy Press Secretary Jahidul Islam Rony. The Power Division and the Infrastructure Development Company Limited (IDCOL) jointly organised the expo for the first time with the theme “Utilise Every Inch of Rooftop, Increase Income through Solar Power”. Chaired by Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Minister Iqbal Hassan Mahmood Tuku, it was also joined by State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Anindya Islam Amit, Finance Secretary Dr Md Khairuzzaman Mozumder and Power Division Secretary Mirana Mahrukh. summary: The American Apparel & Footwear Association (AAFA) has urged the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) to address foreign trade barriers and provide greater certainty in US tarif...
content: The American Apparel & Footwear Association (AAFA) has urged the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR) to address foreign trade barriers and provide greater certainty in US tariff policies. They warn that rising duties and regulatory restrictions are increasing costs for apparel, footwear, and travel goods companies. Figure:Total US tariffs collected on apparel, footwear, and travel goods reached $28.44 billion in 2025, up 68% from $16.89 billion in 2024. In its October 29 submission to the USTR's 2027 National Trade Estimate (NTE) Report on Foreign Trade Barriers, AAFA identified trade-related challenges across 12 countries, including China, India, Japan, Indonesia, Mexico, and Canada. The association said tariffs, customs procedures, technical standards, and import restrictions are disrupting supply chains and limiting market access. Rising tariffs increase industry costs According to data prepared by Trade Partnership Worldwide, LLC, the average trade-weighted tariff rate on US apparel imports increased from 14.70% in 2024 to 24.56% in 2025. Footwear tariffs rose from 12.26% to 23.75%, while travel goods tariffs increased from 13.85% to 22.83%. Total US tariffs collected on apparel, footwear, and travel goods reached $28.44 billion in 2025, up 68% from $16.89 billion in 2024. Through August 2026, the industry had paid another $17.90 billion, including $8.23 billion in additional duties imposed under presidential trade authorities. AAFA said overlapping tariffs under Sections 301, 232, 122, and 338 are making sourcing and long-term planning more difficult. It called for preventing multiple tariffs from applying to the same products, removing duties on manufacturing inputs and machinery, and providing sufficient notice before introducing new measures.

Serving millions of small and medium-sized businesses across Europe, the United States, Canada and Australia, VistaPrint has expanded well beyond its original business card printing activities to offer a wide range of customised products, including apparel, promotional materials, packaging and signage. The company has worked with Israel-headquartered Kornit Digital since 2007, progressively upgrading its digital garment printing operations through successive generations of technology, including the Kornit Atlas and Atlas MAX systems. The latest investment in Apollo represents a further step towards high-volume, on-demand apparel manufacturing, allowing VistaPrint to respond more quickly to incoming orders while reducing the handling and labour requirements associated with garment production. The installation was supported by online training ahead of commissioning and an on-site Kornit technician during the first six months of operation. content: Picanol will introduce a new generation of airjet weaving machines at ITMA Asia + CITME 2026 in Shanghai from November 20–24th, extending its portfolio into the market for basic woven fabrics. The new AirOne loom has been developed specifically for this segment and features a newly designed crank shedding motion, combining high productivity with low energy consumption, advanced digital capabilities and ease of operation. The launch follows extensive market research, R&D and field testing, and represents an important expansion of Picanol’s airjet weaving portfolio. AirOne will complement the established OmniPlus-i Connect, providing mills producing basic fabrics with an alternative designed around their specific production requirements. The machine incorporates a range of Picanol’s existing innovations and patented technologies, with particular emphasis on operational efficiency, sustainability and simplified machine control. “AirOne represents a special launch for Picanol,” says Johan Verstraete, vice president of weaving machines at Picanol. “This new machine platform brings together all the strengths that define Picanol today, from high performance and low energy consumption to digital capabilities and ease of operation. At the Shanghai exhibition, Picanol will demonstrate three machines on its stand F01 in Hall 3. Held from 27-29 October 2026 at the Palais des Festivals in Cannes, the exhibition brought together leading European manufacturers of fabrics and accessories for beachwear, underwear and athleisure. More than 100 collections for Summer 2028 were presented, offering buyers an overview of developments in textile design, material innovation and performance. Despite continuing geopolitical and economic uncertainty, MarediModa reported results in line with the previous year, with no decline in overall activity. Organisers highlighted a more focused approach among visiting buyers, with greater attention to collection development, material selection and planning for future seasons. Claudio Taiana, President of MarediModa, said the results suggested a gradual return to confidence following a period of stagnation. “We had expected this edition to mark an acceleration after a period of stagnation linked to the international geopolitical situation. The Role of International Buyers Building a resilient and sustainable apparel supply chain is a shared responsibility. Dr Rubana Huq, Chairperson of Mohammadi Group, delivered the keynote address, followed by panel discussions led by Md Mahbub ur Rahman, CEO of HSBC Bangladesh, featuring Ranjan Mahtani, Founder and Chairman of Epic Group, Sunny Malhotra, Managing Director of PDS Group, Dr Henry Soo, Managing Director of DataDevelop Consulting, Kim Hellström of H&M and Surendar Singh of Kontoor Brands. Discussions explored Bangladesh’s competitive positioning, evolving global sourcing priorities, product diversification, sustainability and the opportunities to move further up the value chain. content: The number of fashion and textile brands achieving the highest level of sustainable chemical management under the Zero Discharge of Hazardous Chemicals (ZDHC) program increased to 21 in 2026 from 15 in the previous assessment. However, the latest report shows that brands still need to do more to help suppliers solve chemical management problems. Figure: The ZDHC Gateway provides factory-level information on chemical inventory conformance and wastewater performance.Courtesy: Collected The 2026 Brands to Zero Report, independently assessed by KPMG Netherlands, examines how brands manage chemicals through company policies, purchasing practices and supply chains. The program classifies brands into three levels: Pioneer, Accelerator and Champion. More brands collect and monitor chemical data The report shows that more brands are asking their suppliers to provide chemical inventory data. The share requiring suppliers to submit ZDHC InCheck data increased from 75% to 91%. The share of brands monitoring this data also rose from 87% to 91%. ZDHC InCheck helps factories check the chemicals in their inventories against the Manufacturing Restricted Substances List (MRSL). The list sets requirements for chemical formulations used in textile, leather and footwear manufacturing. However, collecting and checking data does not always lead to action. Only 74% of brands follow up with suppliers on the findings, although this figure increased from 60% in the previous assessment. This means that some brands identify chemical management problems but do not consistently follow up to ensure that suppliers address them. content: Dow has launched a new silicone-organic hybrid textile finishing technology designed to provide durable water repellency alongside resistance to oil-based contaminants, without relying on conventional fluorinated chemistry. The new Dowsil IE-5619 DWOR Emulsion has been developed to help textile manufacturers and brands respond to increasingly stringent restrictions on fluorinated substances, while maintaining the performance, comfort and appearance of finished fabrics. Achieving effective oil repellency has traditionally been one of the major challenges in developing alternatives to fluorinated textile finishes. Dow says its third-generation silicone-organic hybrid technology is designed to address this limitation, offering resistance to both water-based stains and a range of oil-based contaminants. The product is intended for use on natural, synthetic and blended fabrics, although performance must be validated for individual fabric types and finishing formulations. The new emulsion can help protect against contaminants including cooking oils, motor oil and sebum, as well as common water-based stains such as coffee, wine and milk. “For years, achieving meaningful oil repellency in textiles typically required fluorinated chemistries, which are now facing increasing restrictions,” said Juan Carlos Medina, global strategic marketing director at Dow. “Dowsil IE-5619 helps close that gap with a silicone-based, fluoro-alternative solution that delivers durable water and oil repellency while preserving the softness, breathability and aesthetics consumers expect.” The new formulation is a 30% solids concentrate designed for integration into conventional textile finishing processes. content: China and India are among the world’s most important textile manufacturing markets and have been key destinations for Swiss textile machinery for decades. Their industrial structures, raw material bases and market dynamics, however, differ considerably. These differences create distinct requirements and opportunities for Swiss suppliers of machinery, components and services. With ITMA Asia + CITME in Shanghai and India ITME in Greater Noida, two major Asian textile machinery exhibitions will take place towards the end of 2026. “China and India are both key markets for our industry, but their industrial environments differ notably,” explains Cornelia Buchwalder, secretary general of Swiss Textile Machinery. “The structure of textile production, the availability of raw materials and the importance of domestic demand all influence their investment priorities. It is also the world’s leading exporter of textiles and apparel, while its substantial domestic market generates significant additional demand. Its position in man-made fibres is particularly strong, with chemical fibre production reaching approximately 87 million tons in 2025. content: Minimum wage enhancement in Bangladesh’s Ready-Made Garment (RMG) sector is economically and socially justified. Rising prices of essential commodities, housing, healthcare, and transportation, coupled with inflation and BDT depreciation, continue to erode workers’ purchasing power. Therefore, nominal wage increases alone cannot ensure improved living standards. A sustainable solution requires coordinated reforms balancing workers’ welfare, industrial competitiveness, and productivity rather than relying solely on periodic wage revisions. Alternative and sustainable solutions Decentralization of factories: Encourage new RMG investments outside Dhaka through improved infrastructure, energy, transport, housing, and targeted incentives. This would reduce living costs, ease pressure on Dhaka, and promote regional development. Regional minimum wages: Introduce a transparent wage structure reflecting regional living costs, particularly housing, food, and transportation, while protecting workers’ basic living standards and ensuring equal pay for comparable work. Minimum wage benchmark in USD: Consider announcing an internationally comparable USD wage benchmark alongside legally guaranteed BDT payments. A transparent conversion mechanism and periodic review should address exchange-rate fluctuations and improve international wage comparisons. Inflation control: Strengthen market monitoring, control artificial price increases, improve supply chains, and stabilize essential commodity prices. content: Italian yarn manufacturer Fulgar has highlighted the potential of bio-based synthetic fibres to reduce the textile industry’s dependence on fossil resources, while emphasising the need for greater transparency, reliable certification and competitive pricing to support their wider adoption. The company contributed to an international discussion on the future of biosynthetics at the recent Performance Days exhibition in Munich, Germany, where Daniela Antunes, Fulgar’s Marketing Manager, joined industry experts to examine the opportunities and challenges associated with renewable raw materials. The panel discussion, entitled From Fossil to Vegetal: The Promises and Challenges of Biosynthetics , brought together representatives from Fulgar, Indorama Ventures, ISCC PLUS and Noosa. Moderated by Sophie Bramel, Technical Editor at Sportstextiles, the session explored the technical, environmental and commercial considerations influencing the development and adoption of biopolymers in textile applications. Central to Fulgar’s contribution was its ongoing research into next-generation polyamide yarns, particularly EVO and Q-GEO, two developments designed to combine renewable raw materials with the performance characteristics required by contemporary textile markets. EVO is a 100% bio-based yarn developed and manufactured by Fulgar using renewable feedstocks derived equally from castor oil and industrial corn. The castor oil originates from crops cultivated in arid regions that do not compete with food production, while the corn component comes from industrial crops not intended for human consumption. content: Swiss automotive supplier Autoneum is to acquire the French Trèves Group in a deal that will significantly expand its global manufacturing operations and strengthen its position in automotive acoustic and thermal insulation, interior trim and luggage compartment solutions. The acquisition will bring together two established suppliers to the international automotive industry, creating a business with combined annual revenues expected to exceed CHF 2.9 billion (€3.1 billion) in 2026. The company has longstanding relationships with major automotive manufacturers and specialises in acoustic and thermal management systems and interior components. Under the agreement announced on November 2nd, Autoneum will pay approximately €40 million upfront, with a further performance-related payment of up to €24 million possible depending on improvements in profitability and the achievement of synergies by 2029. The shares will be subject to a three-year lock-up period. The transaction is expected to be completed in early 2027, subject to consultation with the relevant employee representative bodies and customary regulatory approvals. summary: Product authentication has been luxury's primary use case for blockchain, but so far it's focused on visibility at the point of sale or resale. Sophisticated CRM systems, loyalty programs, and digital analytics give them a precise picture of purchasing behaviours, spending patterns, and customer preferences. Brands and maisons know, in exacting detail, who their best clients are, what they buy, how often they shop, and what they are likely to want next. They use this to put some of the world’s most sophisticated clienteling operations into practice, for the planet’s most discerning shoppers. What they have comparatively little visibility into is what happens to the products they buy after the point of sale, and the extended lives those products (which are uniquely designed for longevity, timeless style, and are seen as a store of value) now live. content: The Institution of Textile Engineers and Technologists (ITET) Bangladesh has called for urgent government action to restore stability and strengthen industrial security amid rising labour unrest in the textile and RMG sector. The organization stressed the need for uninterrupted production to safeguard Bangladesh’s key export industry and maintain investor confidence. In a statement, ITET Bangladesh expressed deep concern over recent incidents of arson, vandalism, labour unrest, protests and road blockades in different industrial areas, saying these incidents have severely disrupted normal factory operations and production. The organization noted that many factories have already shut down, raising concerns over the country's economy, employment and export trade. According to ITET Bangladesh, the industry was attempting to recover from prolonged gas crises and other challenges when the fresh wave of instability created further uncertainty about its future. It also warned that continued unrest could undermine the confidence of international buyers and investors and damage Bangladesh's image in the global market. Emphasizing the importance of protecting workers' legitimate rights and demands, ITET Bangladesh said factory security, a stable production environment and the rule of law must also be ensured. The organization called for resolving the underlying causes of labour unrest through dialogue between workers and factory owners. content: On November 1, the Bangladesh government has formed a new wage board to determine revised minimum wages for readymade garment (RMG) workers amid ongoing labor unrest and demands for a monthly minimum wage of Tk 30,000. The six-member board, constituted under the Ministry of Labour and Employment, is chaired by Sheikh Ashfaqur Rahman, a senior district and sessions judge. The board includes five members representing employers, workers and the independent category. Prof. Mosleh Uddin Ahmed of the Department of Public Administration at the University of Dhaka has been appointed as the independent member. Employer representatives include Asif Ayub, Joint Secretary-General of the Bangladesh Employers’ Federation, and A.B.M. Shamsuddin, Director of the Bangladesh Garment Manufacturers and Exporters Association (BGMEA). Worker representatives are Anwar Hossain, President of Bangladesh Jatiyatabadi Sramik Dal, and Babul Akhter, General Secretary of the Bangladesh Garments and Industrial Workers Federation. The appointments were announced through separate notifications issued under the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006, as amended in 2026. The chairman has been instructed to initiate the process of fixing the minimum wage in consultation with all stakeholders. Labour and Employment Minister Ariful Haque Choudhury announced the formation of the board, stating that it has been tasked with recommending a revised wage structure within six months. The review comes three years after the last wage revision in 2023, when the minimum monthly wage for garment workers was set at Tk 12,500. content: Key Insights Bangladesh RMG sector faces a $4.8 billion funding gap to meet 2030 climate goals. Australian clean energy delegations explore battery storage partnerships to stabilize factory power. Denmark and Sweden support a 500 MW offshore wind project off Cox's Bazar. Natural gas shortages and LNG spot prices near $30 per MMBtu raise operational costs. Rooftop solar cannot power wet processing, requiring heat recovery and electrification. Bangladesh's ready-made garment industry is partnering with global fashion brands, renewable energy companies, and international development partners to adopt solar power, offshore wind, battery storage, and energy-efficient machinery. Manufacturers are making this shift to handle high energy costs, gas shortages, and strict carbon reduction demands from international buyers. However, realizing this green transition requires substantial capital expenditure. According to LightCastle Partners, Bangladesh's RMG sector requires $6.6 billion between 2025 and 2029 to achieve a 50 percent reduction in greenhouse gas emissions by 2030. With only $1.6 billion in funding secured to date, the sector faces a massive $4.8 billion financing gap that demands urgent expansion of international climate finance, soft loans, and concessionary funding mechanisms. To bridge the financial shortfall and accelerate on-site clean energy, international solar investments and technology transfers are expanding rapidly across Bangladesh's apparel sector. Denmark's Heartland and fashion giant BESTSELLER are funding solar decarbonization models through a partnership with local cleantech venture SOLshare. content: Garment workers staged fresh protests in several areas of Gazipur on Sunday, demanding an increase in the minimum monthly wage to Tk30,000. The demonstrations and road blockades brought traffic on the Dhaka–Tangail Highway to a standstill, while protesters set fire to a police box in Konabari. Five platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel have been deployed to maintain law and order amid the unrest. On the morning of 01 November, workers took to the streets in Safipur Bazar, Chandra Palli Bidyut, Mouchak and Telichala areas of Kaliakair upazila, staging demonstrations and chanting slogans demanding higher wages. According to Kaliakair Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Shahidul Islam, workers had occupied the highway since morning, disrupting traffic on the busy route. Gazipur Deputy Commissioner Md. Nurul Karim Bhuiyan said five platoons of BGB personnel had been deployed in view of the situation. The number could be increased if necessary. In Konabari, agitated workers set fire to a police box located in the middle of the highway. They reportedly removed items from the police box and set those on fire as well, said Konabari Police Station OC Iftekhar Hossain. The protests come after nearly two weeks of demonstrations by garment workers in different parts of Gazipur over wage increases. On 31 October, workers blocked the highway around Chandra Palli Bidyut and Gate No. 3 of the Ansar Academy in Kaliakair until around 8:30 pm. Police later dispersed them using tear gas and batons. Traffic returned to normal after nearly five hours. content: Danish garment maker Spectre has inaugurated a new green factory in Hung Yen Province, northern Vietnam, expanding its manufacturing footprint in the country while helping reduce greenhouse gas emissions through energy-efficient production, according to the Danish Embassy in Vietnam. The new facility, Spectre Hung Yen 2, opened at Song Tra Industrial Park in Thai Binh Ward on Friday, marking the company’s fourth factory in Vietnam and second in Hung Yen. With nearly 80 years of experience in the garment industry, Spectre specializes in producing functional apparel for premium sportswear and outdoor brands. Backed by an investment of US$30 million, the new factory is expected to cut carbon dioxide emissions by approximately 1,600 metric tons annually compared with conventional factories of a similar size. It has received LEED Gold certification, the third-highest certification level under the Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) rating system developed by the U.S. Green Building Council. The facility combines solar power with modern design solutions to improve energy efficiency and reduce its environmental footprint. It is also equipped with advanced machinery and technologies, including automation and artificial intelligence (AI) solutions, to improve production efficiency and establish higher standards across Spectre’s manufacturing operations. The factory is expected to create jobs for around 3,000 local workers. Jesper Klausen, Spectre’s co-owner and chief business development officer, said the company, was proud of its latest investment in Hung Yen. The International Energy Agency (IEA) had also urged its member countries in mid-October to increase oil supplies from strategic reserves ahead of the winter season.
